claims.text: Post-SLM deep cryogenic treatment with gradual rewarming will improve the dimensional precision of CoCrFeNiMn components.
Post-SLM deep cryogenic treatment with gradual rewarming will improve the mechanical integrity of CoCrFeNiMn components.
The proposed treatment will reduce residual stresses in SLM-fabricated CoCrFeNiMn.
The proposed treatment will heal microstructural defects without causing thermal shock or additional microcracking.
SLM-fabricated CoCrFeNiMn components exhibit residual stresses, microporosity, warpage, and dislocation irregularities.
The intervention consists of immediate post-fabrication immersion in liquid nitrogen at -196 °C for 12 hours followed by controlled gradual rewarming to room temperature.
A CoCrFeNiMn-specific optimized rewarming schedule can permit beneficial microstructural transformations while avoiding new defects.
Deep cryogenic treatment will refine and homogenize the CoCrFeNiMn microstructure.
Microporosity will be healed through dislocation rearrangement and nanotwinning.
Deep cryogenic treatment induces rapid lattice contraction in CoCrFeNiMn.
Gradual rewarming after cryogenic contraction facilitates stress relaxation in CoCrFeNiMn.
The treatment promotes nanotwin formation and rearrangement of the dislocation lattice.
Stress relaxation and microstructural reorganization reduce internal microporosity and residual thermal stress.
Relative to untreated SLM parts, treated components will exhibit less warpage and smaller dimensional deviations.
Relative to untreated SLM parts, treated components will exhibit higher tensile strength.
Relative to untreated SLM parts, treated components will exhibit improved ductility.
Relative to untreated SLM parts, treated components will have fewer fabrication-induced defects.
Internal SLM defects and residual-stress-driven deformation can impair dimensional accuracy and mechanical performance.
